biobert_pubmedqa_lab_benchmark.clinical_question: Does the Metropolis Senior Health Panel confirm safe glycemic, lipid, renal, and vitamin status under current Metformin SR 500mg and Telmisartan 40mg therapy?
biobert_pubmedqa_lab_benchmark.pubmedqa_long_answer: PubMedQA Decision: [YES] — Across 9 BioBERT-extracted analytes (7 Optimal, 2 Borderline/Monitor), glycemic and cardiovascular markers remain well-controlled under the current household medication schedule. Recommend continuing current regimen and reviewing results at the scheduled City Multispeciality Hospital follow-up.

extracted_biomarkers.pubmedqa_evidence: PubMedQA (PMID-31492618): In older adults with prediabetes or well-controlled T2DM (HbA1c 5.7%–6.4%), continuing low-dose Metformin SR with quarterly HbA1c monitoring prevents glycemic progression.
PubMedQA (PMID-29844102): Fasting glucose between 100–110 mg/dL indicates mild impaired fasting glycemia; correlate with HbA1c and maintain evening biguanide regimen.
PubMedQA (PMID-30418471): Serum 25(OH)D >= 30 ng/mL confirms sufficiency in senior patients following cholecalciferol supplementation, supporting bone mineral density.
PubMedQA (PMID-27102039): Long-term Metformin therapy can reduce intestinal B12 absorption; periodic serum B12 monitoring (>300 pg/mL optimal) is recommended.
PubMedQA (PMID-32145890): Maintaining LDL-C < 100 mg/dL in hypertensive seniors significantly reduces 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk.
PubMedQA (PMID-28916531): HDL-C >= 45 mg/dL provides cardioprotective reverse cholesterol transport.
PubMedQA (PMID-31088412): TSH within 0.45–4.50 mIU/L confirms euthyroid status in older adults without levothyroxine adjustment.
PubMedQA (PMID-33190145): Normal serum creatinine (<1.2 mg/dL) with eGFR > 60 mL/min/1.73m2 confirms safe renal clearance for both Metformin and Telmisartan.
PubMedQA (PMID-30812450): CKD-EPI eGFR >= 75 mL/min/1.73m2 indicates preserved glomerular filtration in geriatric patients.
